identity.title: POCUS lung: absent lung sliding (+/- lung point, absent B-lines) for pneumothorax

technique.how: Supine patient; high-frequency linear (or curvilinear/phased) probe longitudinal on the anterior chest at the 2nd-4th interspace midclavicular line, then several other anterior/lateral points. Identify the pleural line between rib shadows and look for sliding in B-mode and 'seashore' vs 'barcode' (stratosphere) sign on M-mode; scan laterally for a lung point.
technique.prerequisites: Patient supine or semi-recumbent (air rises anteriorly); operator credentialed in lung POCUS; interpretation in the clinical context.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay needle decompression in tension pneumothorax to scan.

interpretation.positive_finding: Absent lung sliding with A-lines and no B-lines or lung pulse at the anterior chest; a lung point (sliding alternating with absent sliding at one location) is specific and confirms pneumothorax.
interpretation.negative_finding: Presence of lung sliding, B-lines or a lung pulse at the scanned interspace rules out pneumothorax at that point; scan multiple points to cover the anterior chest.
interpretation.pitfalls: Sliding is also absent with mainstem intubation, apnea, pleural adhesions, ARDS, bullae and prior pleurodesis, so absent sliding alone is not diagnostic. Sensitivity is much lower in novice/prehospital hands and for small or loculated pneumothoraces.
interpretation.changes_what: Absent sliding plus lung point in a dyspneic/hypotensive patient: treat as pneumothorax (decompress if unstable); sliding at all anterior points makes significant pneumothorax unlikely.

estimates.target_condition: Pneumothorax (absence of lung sliding and comet-tail artifacts)
estimates.population: Adults clinically suspected of pneumothorax (trauma and post-procedure), 8 studies, 1,048 patients; mostly emergency physicians/intensivists
estimates.reference_standard: CT scan or release of air on chest tube placement
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.909/(1-0.982) = 50.5; LR- = (1-0.909)/0.982 = 0.093, from pooled sensitivity 90.9% and specificity 98.2%
estimates.quote: Ultrasonography was 90.9% sensitive (95% CI, 86.5-93.9) and 98.2% specific (95% CI, 97.0-99.0) for the detection of pneumothorax.

estimates.population: Adults evaluated for pneumothorax, subgroup of studies with clinician (non-radiologist) operators
estimates.reference_standard: CT or chest tube findings (per included studies)
estimates.quote: For ultrasonography performed by clinicians other than radiologists, pooled sensitivity and specificity were 0.89 and 0.99, respectively.

estimates.target_condition: Pneumothorax (anterior absent lung sliding + A-lines + lung point, BLUE 'A prime' profile)
estimates.population: 260 consecutive ICU admissions with acute respiratory failure and definite diagnosis; 9 pneumothorax; single expert operator
estimates.quote: Anterior absent lung sliding plus A lines plus lung point indicated pneumothorax (n=9) with 81% sensitivity and 100% specificity.

estimates.target_condition: Pneumothorax (thoracic POCUS by HEMS/prehospital providers, mostly novice nurses/paramedics)
estimates.population: Medical and trauma patients scanned prehospital/in helicopter; 8 studies, 1,713 images
estimates.quote: pooled sensitivity 61% (95% CI: 27-87%; I2 = 94%) and pooled specificity 99% (95% CI: 98-100%; I2 = 89%)

sources.citation: Alrajhi K, Woo MY, Vaillancourt C. Test characteristics of ultrasonography for the detection of pneumothorax: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Chest. 2012;141(3):703-708.
Ding W, Shen Y, Yang J, He X, Zhang M. Diagnosis of pneumothorax by radiography and ultrasonography: a meta-analysis. Chest. 2011;140(4):859-866.
Lichtenstein DA, Meziere GA. Relevance of lung ultrasound in the diagnosis of acute respiratory failure: the BLUE protocol. Chest. 2008;134(1):117-125.
Griffiths E. Helicopter emergency medical services use of thoracic point of care ultrasound for pneumothorax: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Scand J Trauma Resusc Emerg Med. 2021;29:163.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absent sliding alone to diagnose pneumothorax in intubated, apneic, post-pleurodesis or severe-ARDS patients; do not use a single-point scan to exclude pneumothorax.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Absent sliding with hypotension or rising airway pressures is presumed tension pneumothorax: decompress immediately rather than completing the scan.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Ding 2011 meta-regression found operator skill strongly associated with accuracy (relative DOR 0.21, 95% CI 0.05-0.96); Griffiths 2021 shows sensitivity falls to 61% with novice prehospital operators.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Assumes an operator trained to basic lung POCUS competency (able to identify the pleural line, sliding, M-mode seashore/barcode, B-lines and lung point); pooled numbers come mainly from emergency physicians and intensivists, not novices.

extraction_notes: Primary estimate from Alrajhi 2012 abstract (Chest, not open access; sens/spec with CIs are in the abstract); LRs computed from the pooled point estimates and flagged computed. Ding 2011 clinician-operator subgroup from abstract (no CIs given there). BLUE profile numbers from Lichtenstein 2008 abstract; prevalence not entered because the cohort excluded uncertain/rare diagnoses. Griffiths 2021 added to show the operator/setting effect on sensitivity; 'setting' recorded as mixed because the schema has no prehospital value. eFAST trauma pooled estimate (Netherton 2019: 69% sensitivity, 99% specificity) was seen but not entered to stay within source budget.
